full_judgment: 8. In that view of the matter the learned Magistrate passed the final order to the effect that the 2nd party No. 2 and 3rd party No. 1 namely Momtaz & Bntaz, successor-In-interest of Namizuddin would remain in possession of the proceeding land until evicted from the land and that the Receiver will hand over the proceeding land to them and they will get the sale proceed which was deposited in this case. As against that a revisional application being Criminal Revision No. 709 of 1978 was moved before this High Court Division and it was heard by a Single Bench by this Court and his Lordships of the Single Bench after hearing the Criminal Revision found that the learned Magistrate rightly held as to possession of the disputed land at the time of drawing up proceeding and in view of the matter his Lordship found no reason to interfere with the order of the learned Magistrate and the Rule was discharged. It appears from records, as exhibited before this court in a supplementary affidavit filed by the opposite party No. 1 Entaz Shaikh and others that thereafter Moslemuddin Halder not found in possession did file a suit for partition and khas possession of the disputed land being T.S. 291 of 1982 in the court of learned Munsif impleading Namizuddin Shaikh being dead, his heir Montaz Shaikh, Entaz Shaikh as a party and in that suit he prayed for partition claiming the land covered by proceeding under section 145 Cr.P.C. to be a co-sharers property and asked for declaration of the Shah am of the parties after partition. He also prayed for title and khas possession and also for mesne profit for 3 years from before the date of filing of the suit till the date of delivery of possession of the suitland. This title suit No. 291/82 covers the land which is under the order of attachment passed again under section 145 Cr P.C. by the learned Magistrate which was again initiated on an application filed by Harunor Rashid alias Fatik who is the younger brother of Moslemuddin and others who bad filed the Title Suit No. 292/92 which is now pending. It is also seen from the earlier proceeding drawn up under section 145 Cr.P.C. concerning the same land that it was a case between the same party claiming pattani right. It was the case of Moslemuddin and his brother that he alongwith his brother Harunor Rashid the present petitioner before this court in Revision and others took settlement of the proceeding laud from the original owner Anil Kumar Basuand had been in possession and it was the successor-in-interest of the heirs of Namizuddin who had always been threatening, causing serious breach of peace. It thus appears that over the selfsame property there were proceeding u/s. 145 Cr. P.C. which were subsequently dropped and lastly it was clearly dropped on a finding that Nizamuddin and his heirs were in possession of the disputed property although and that finding was ultimately confirmed by this court in Criminal Revision No. 125 of 1968. Yet, again another proceeding under section 145 if the Code of Criminal, Procedure was drawn over the same land this time on the application of Harunor Rashid, a full brother or Moslemuddin.
